📒 *known issue recurrence* — `ki-2026-07-04-crm-amqp-consumer-monitor-family-quiet-period-flap`
This is occurrence #175 (lifetime; the 11-19 catch-up after the 56-day gap means a clean 7-day count isn't available).
Owning team (would tag — not tagged): `Vertical App Experience` (`sales management` usergroup / `#team-sales-management`)
Playbook: confirm the dip is a genuine brief drop below the monitor floor (not a data gap), confirm 0 `status:error` logs, treat as quiet-period noise.
Open Jira: none

Source alerts (1 total): monitor 302057011 `[CRM] runtime-core-subscriber throughput dropped (possible stall)`, transition 2026-11-20T03:32:31Z (recovery edge, OK at scan). Degraded cycle (Slack MCP unavailable), so no permalink.

Root-cause analysis:
  • `sum:trace.amqp.command.hits{service:runtime-core-subscriber,env:prod}.as_rate()` 01:30–05:00Z: 210 points; 15-min windows below the 2 msg/s floor ~02:23–03:30Z (overnight quiet period), min 0.35/s @03:43Z, then back to normal (max 182/s @04:11Z).
  • `service:runtime-core-subscriber status:error` 02:00–05:00Z: 0 logs.
  • Reasoning: a real but harmless overnight low-traffic dip on a fixed-floor threshold, matching the KB shape. Not a consumer stall.
  • Sibling 302055141 (mobile-notifications heartbeat, 04:20Z) matched the same entry this cycle (occ #176) and was suppressed by the 24h window this post reset. That's an ordering artifact, see its report.

Evidence:
  • DD metric: https://app.datadoghq.com/metric/explorer?live=false&page=0&exp_metric=trace.amqp.command.hits&exp_scope=service%3Aruntime-core-subscriber%2Cenv%3Aprod&exp_agg=avg&start=1795138200&end=1795150800
  • DD monitor: https://app.datadoghq.com/monitors/302057011
Report: docs/investigations/2026-11-20-3ddfa9c1e3bce5fd.md

📒 *known issue recurrence* — `ki-2026-07-07-notifications-p95-latency-monitor-noise`
This is occurrence #50 (lifetime). 50 fires so far and none has reproduced.
Owning team (would tag — not tagged): `CRM Experience` (`customer-management` usergroup / `#team-customer-management`)
Playbook: re-query p95 over the monitor's own window plus a wider one (expect 0.001–0.2s, nowhere near 1s), confirm 0 error logs, don't treat as user-impacting.
Open Jira: none

Source alerts (1 total): monitor 302056327 `[CRM][P2] notifications P95 latency high`, transition 2026-11-20T09:43:07Z (OK at scan). Degraded cycle, so no permalink.

Root-cause analysis:
  • `p95:trace.aspnet.request{service:notifications,env:prod}` 09:00–10:15Z: 150 points, max 0.618s @09:30Z, *0 points over the 1s threshold*.
  • `service:notifications status:error` 09:20–09:50Z: 0 logs. Traffic normal (hits max 688/interval @09:30Z).
  • Reasoning: the breach doesn't show up in the metric the monitor evaluates, so this is the known monitor/data artifact. Suggest retuning or muting this monitor.

Evidence:
  • DD metric (p95): https://app.datadoghq.com/metric/explorer?live=false&page=0&exp_metric=trace.aspnet.request&exp_scope=service%3Anotifications%2Cenv%3Aprod&exp_agg=avg&start=1795165200&end=1795169700
  • DD monitor: https://app.datadoghq.com/monitors/302056327
Report: docs/investigations/2026-11-20-97042596ab37709f.md

📒 *known issue recurrence* — `ki-2026-07-03-eda-consumer-amqp-stopped-publishing`
This is occurrence #73 (lifetime). The previous one was the 10:34Z fire, which was suppressed. This is a new gap.
Owning team (would tag — not tagged): `Integrations` (EDA stack; no Teams row, so no handle)
Playbook: 1) Confirm 296641466 is No Data. 2) Check sibling P1s 296632224 (event ingest) and 296636101 (Kafka produce): both OK means the EDA core is healthy. 3) Confirm service:eda_consumer status:error = 0. 4) Escalate only if the sibling P1s are also firing.
Open Jira: none

Source alerts (1 total): monitor 296641466 went No Data at 2026-11-20T11:22:26+00:00 (degraded cycle: Slack MCP unavailable, so no permalink). Still No Data at the 12:07Z scan.

Root-cause analysis:
  • `sum:trace.amqp.command.hits{service:eda_consumer,env:prod}.as_count()` in 5-minute buckets: 817 (10:35Z), 908, 475, 64 (10:50Z), then *no datapoints 10:55Z–12:08Z* (~75min and still open).
  • Hourly: same burst-then-lull shape as 11-19 (09–10Z: 1661/2212, then 23 at 11Z). Today the 11Z hour is empty, so the gap is longer than yesterday's.
  • Sibling P1s 296632224/296636101 have been OK since 11-13. DD Logs `service:eda_consumer status:error` 10:00–12:08Z = 0.
  • Verdict: the bursty consumer went quiet after its morning batch and tripped `sum(last_30m) < 1`. No sign of a pipeline outage. If the gap is still open in the next cycle, it is worth a look.
  • Gate note: last notified 2026-11-19T11:29Z. That is 24h38m by the cycle-eval anchor (posted on that basis) but 23h53m by fire timestamp.

Evidence:
  • DD metric: https://app.datadoghq.com/metric/explorer?live=false&page=0&exp_metric=trace.amqp.command.hits&exp_scope=service%3Aeda_consumer%2Cenv%3Aprod&exp_agg=avg&start=1795167000&end=1795176497
  • DD monitor: https://app.datadoghq.com/monitors/296641466
  • Kibana: not the evidence datasource for this KB (datadog_apm)
Report: docs/investigations/2026-11-20-c7c1dba5d8dc97b3.md
